hints: Look at the final ester and work backwards, an ester is made from which two functional groups?
Identify X and Y first. Both come from the same 3-carbon nitrile, so X must be propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$.
Think about how to change a carboxylic acid into a primary alcohol. Which powerful reducing agent can do this while the other common one cannot?
walkthrough:
**Identify X and Y from the ester**

Ester formation needs a carboxylic acid plus an alcohol. For $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, split at the $\text{CO}_2$ group.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Work out step 1, nitrile to acid**

Starting material $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$ has 3 carbons, same as X. Acid hydrolysis of a nitrile gives the carboxylic acid directly.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{HCl(aq), heat}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$
So X is propanoic acid, and step 1 needs $\text{HCl(aq)}$.

**Work out step 2, acid to alcohol**

X (propanoic acid) must be converted to Y (propan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$). This is a reduction of a carboxylic acid to a primary alcohol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$
Only $\text{LiAlH}_4$ is strong enough. Step 3 is then normal esterification of X + Y.

options.A: Step 1 is correct, $\text{HCl(aq)}$ does give propanoic acid. Step 2 is wrong because conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is a dehydrating agent and catalyst for esterification, not a reducing agent, so it cannot reduce the acid to propan-1-ol.
options.B: Step 1 with $\text{HCl(aq)}$ gives X as propanoic acid by acid hydrolysis. Step 2 with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ reduces the acid to Y as propan-1-ol. X + Y then esterify in step 3 to give propyl propanoate. This fits perfectly.
options.C: Step 1 with $\text{NaOH(aq)}$ gives the carboxylate salt, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$, not the free acid needed for esterification. Step 2 with conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ also cannot reduce a carboxyl group to an alcohol.
options.D: Step 1 again gives only the sodium salt, not propanoic acid. Step 2 is also wrong because $\text{NaBH}_4$ is too mild to reduce a carboxylic acid, it only reduces aldehydes and ketones, so Y would never form.
